In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thrombotic process is a complex phenomenon that involves many factors and mechanisms, and the role of the coagulation system is not limited only to thrombus formation.
the thrombosis and hemostasis system is a complex and highly regulated network of proteins that are involved in the control of blood coagulation and fibrinolysis.
the platelet is a cell with an active metabolism that has the ability to respond to external stimuli and to interact with other cells and with the extracellular matrix.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the platelet is the first responder to vascular injury and is the first line of defence against blood loss.
we have identified a number of novel proteins and mechanisms that are involved in hemostasis and thrombosis.
we are interested in how the blood vessel wall, and the blood flowing through it, interact to regulate the formation of the platelet plug.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the platelet is a dynamic, highly plastic, cell with an enormous potential to respond to changes in its environment.
the platelet plug is a dynamic entity that undergoes continuous remodeling and maturation in response to local cues.
the platelet plug is a dynamic entity, which can be remodeled to allow the passage of leukocytes and red blood cells through the plug, thereby allowing blood flow to resume.
